run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p', run a `range: { "@timestamp": { gte: "2026-06-03T00:00:00" } }` query filtered to level=ERROR and tell me the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: The query ran inside index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p. The index exists (green, 16 documents) but its mapping has no @timestamp field at all: the only mapped fields are ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text). Elasticsearch did not error on the requested range on @timestamp; it correctly matched zero documents, so the requested count is 0. Re-running the same range condition against the field that actually carries the log time, ingest_ts (gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00), combined with level=ERROR returned 7. For context, the whole index holds 12 ERROR documents (5 at 2026-06-02T08:01:00–08:05:00 and 7 at 2026-06-03T08:01:00–08:07:00) and 4 INFO documents at 2026-06-03T09:01:00–09:04:00; the 7 counted are exactly the 2026-06-03 ERROR documents. Important limits: ingest_ts is a keyword, not a date field, so the tool applied no time filter and these documents cannot be proven to fall inside the authorized window (2026-11-21T10:32:18Z to 2026-11-22T10:32:18Z); the counts describe the index's stored documents, not the incident window.

claims.text: Index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p exists and is green with docs.count 16 and store.size 6.5kb, and its mapping contains only ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text) — there is no @timestamp field and no date-typed field.

The query exactly as asked — bool{range @timestamp gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00 AND term level=ERROR} on app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p — returned status ok, no shard failures, and total = 0 (relation eq), not an error.
Re-running the same range condition on the field that actually holds the log time, ingest_ts (keyword), with range gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00 plus term level=ERROR, returned total = 7.

ingest_ts is typed keyword, not date, so the tool reports time_filter applied=false and the returned documents cannot be proven to belong to the authorized window 2026-11-21T10:32:18Z–2026-11-22T10:32:18Z; the counts describe stored documents, not the incident window.

Whole-index listing and a terms aggregation on ingest_ts for level=ERROR show 12 ERROR documents in total: 5 at 2026-06-02T08:01:00, 08:02:00, 08:03:00, 08:04:00, 08:05:00 and 7 at 2026-06-03T08:01:00, 08:02:00, 08:03:00, 08:04:00, 08:05:00, 08:06:00, 08:07:00 (sum_other_doc_count 0). The remaining 4 documents are level=INFO at 2026-06-03T09:01:00–09:04:00, so 12 ERROR + 4 INFO accounts for all 16 documents.

gaps: The requested @timestamp range cannot be evaluated as a time range at all: no @timestamp field (and no date-typed field) exists in app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p, so the value 0 for that query reflects only a field-name mismatch and says nothing about how many ERROR logs exist in that period.
ingest_ts is keyword, so the 7-document count could not be confined to the authorized window; whether these 2026-06-02/06-03 documents relate to the 2026-11-21/22 incident window is unknown.
Completeness of the index is unknown: it holds only 16 documents, and retention, ingest delay or index selection could leave gaps that neither the mapping nor the counts can rule out.
The message field of the ERROR documents was not read (only ingest_ts and level were projected), so the content and cause of those ERROR lines remain unknown.
next_steps: If period-accurate counting is needed, confirm the intended time field and, if it must be range-queried, whether it can be mapped as a date field (ingest_ts is currently keyword and only works lexicographically because values are ISO-8601).

Re-run the count against a window that actually contains these documents (2026-06-02 to 2026-06-03) or against an index whose logs cover the authorized window before drawing any incident-window conclusion.
